title: Best Wireless Earbuds UK
short: True wireless earbuds compared by noise cancelling, battery life and sound quality, from budget to premium.
intro: Wireless earbuds range from sub-£50 budget picks to premium models with lossless audio and spatial sound. This guide compares earbuds tested by Expert Reviews, whose reviewers say they have tested over 300 pairs in the past five years, so you can match the features to what you actually use them for.

products.name: WF-1000XM6
products.best_for: Buyers who want the strongest all-round package
products.summary: Expert Reviews' overall winner. It combines superb noise cancelling with excellent audio quality and an extensive feature set.

products.name: Melomania A100
products.best_for: Buyers who want high-end sound specs without the high-end price
products.key_spec: 39hr battery, LDAC and aptX Lossless, IPX5
products.summary: Detailed, effective-sounding earbuds with noise cancelling and specs that punch above their price. Expert Reviews notes the bass integration is only average.

products.name: Buds 2
products.best_for: Buyers on a tight budget who still want ANC
products.summary: A feature-rich budget pair with noise cancelling, spatial audio and a gaming mode, though the ANC has limitations and there's no hi-res codec support.

products.name: EAH-AZ100
products.best_for: Buyers who switch between several devices during the day
products.summary: Class-leading multipoint pairing across three devices, with strong sound quality and call clarity, though the eartip selection is limited.

products.name: QuietComfort Ultra Earbuds (2nd Gen)
products.best_for: Buyers who prioritise blocking out noise above all else
products.summary: Expert Reviews' pick for noise cancelling, with a comfortable fit and immersive spatial sound, though battery life is only average for the category.

products.name: AirPods Pro 3
products.best_for: iPhone owners who make a lot of calls
products.summary: Expert Reviews rates these highest for call quality, with strong ANC and a comfortable design, though pure audio quality trails some rivals.
cons: Audio quality could improve versus rivals

products.name: OpenFit 2 Plus
products.best_for: Runners and gym-goers who want to stay aware of their surroundings
products.summary: An open-ear design that sits outside the ear canal, with loud and punchy audio and a lightweight feel, though bass is modest and codec support limited.

products.name: Powerbeats Pro 2
products.best_for: Gym and running use where a secure fit matters
products.key_spec: 45hr battery, earhook design, heart rate sensor
products.summary: An earhook design built for a stable fit during exercise, with heart rate tracking and excellent battery life, though ANC affects audio quality.
cons: IPX4 is a lower water resistance rating

guide.q: Do I need active noise cancelling (ANC)?
guide.a: ANC is worth it for commuting, flying or working in a noisy space. If you mainly use earbuds at home or for exercise outdoors where awareness of your surroundings matters, it is less essential, and an open-ear design like the Shokz may suit you better.

guide.q: What do the codec names (LDAC, aptX) mean?
guide.a: These are ways of sending higher-quality audio over Bluetooth. They only make an audible difference if your phone also supports the same codec and you are listening to high-quality audio files or streams, so check your phone's compatibility before paying extra for them.

guide.q: What do the IP water-resistance ratings mean?
guide.a: The number after IP indicates resistance to solids and liquids, for example IPX4 resists splashes and sweat, while IP55 and higher resist more sustained exposure. None of the earbuds here are rated for swimming or submersion.

guide.q: How much battery life do I actually need?
guide.a: Look at the total battery life including the charging case, not just a single charge. For daily commuting or office use, 20-plus hours total is usually enough to go several days between charges.
